definition: The most vulgar Arabic slang term for the vagina; the primary sexual expletive and taboo word for female genitalia across the Arab world.
notes: Arguably the single most offensive word in Arabic; cognate with similar roots across Semitic languages; functions simultaneously as expletive, insult, and sexual noun; recognized by virtually all adult Arabic speakers regardless of dialect.

definition: Regional crude slang for the vagina; less universal than كس but well understood in Levantine and some Egyptian dialect zones.
notes: May derive from the root بصص (to stare/peek), creating a voyeuristic spatial metaphor; recognition drops substantially outside Levantine and Egyptian dialect zones.

definition: Dialectal phonological variant of كس; crude slang for the vagina with the same vulgar force as the base form, widely used in Egyptian, Levantine, and Mesopotamian Arabic.
notes: Near-synonym of كس differing only in vowel pattern; carries essentially identical crude register; more common in Egyptian and Levantine varieties than in Gulf Arabic.

definition: Crude slang for the vagina literally meaning 'hole' or 'pit'; dehumanizes by reducing female genitalia to a penetrable cavity.
notes: The 'hole' metaphor for vagina is cross-linguistically common; crude through reductionism rather than phonetic taboo; primary literal meaning is excavation pit or ditch.

definition: Crude slang for the vagina meaning 'abyss,' 'chasm,' or 'void'; extends the depth metaphor beyond حفرة to its most extreme spatial form.
notes: Primary meaning is 'precipice' or 'abyss'; its use as vagina slang amplifies the spatial/depth metaphor; less widely recognized as a genital term than other entries in this set.

definition: Crude slang for the vagina based on the meaning 'crack' or 'split'; references the visible labial cleft as the defining feature.
notes: Shares orthography with the modern colloquial Arabic word for 'apartment' (شقة, from the same root شق meaning to split apart); dual meaning enables crude wordplay in everyday speech.

definition: Crude slang for the vagina or vaginal opening meaning 'aperture' or 'opening'; the least phonetically taboo of the hole-based terms due to its neutral literal root.
notes: Shares orthography with the Arabic diacritical mark فتحة (the short 'a' vowel); anatomically closer to vaginal opening than the vaginal canal proper; the clinical neutrality of the root word tempers crudeness relative to كس.

definition: The standard classical and clinical Arabic term for the clitoris; used in medical texts, anatomical literature, and formal health discourse across the Arab world.
notes: Documented in medieval Islamic medical literature (Ibn Sina); appears prominently in FGM/female circumcision (ختان الإناث) discourse; carries social taboo in lay speech despite clinical status, causing many speakers to avoid saying it aloud publicly.

definition: A clinical Arabic variant of بظر for the clitoris using the feminine noun form; appears in gynecological and anatomical texts as an alternate standard term.
notes: Morphological feminine-form variant of بظر; used interchangeably with the base form in medical contexts; slightly lower lay recognition than بظر; the feminine suffix -ة may reflect anatomical naming conventions adapted from classical sources.

definition: A descriptive anatomical term for the clitoris literally meaning 'the protuberance' or 'the bump'; used in Arabic health education materials as a morphologically transparent alternative to بظر.
notes: The word حدبة also describes any bodily hump, including kyphosis; the clitoral sense requires anatomical context; lower recognition than بظر among lay speakers; more common in health education materials than specialist clinical texts.

definition: The highly technical anatomical Arabic term for the clitoral corpus cavernosum; the paired erectile tissue columns forming the internal body of the clitoris.
notes: al-jism al-kahfī (the cavernous body) + al-baẓrī (clitoral, adjectival form of بظر); essentially zero lay recognition; used only in anatomy education, gynecology, and sexual medicine literature.

definition: The most common colloquial Arabic slang for the clitoris, literally meaning 'button'; widely understood across dialects with moderate rather than extreme crudeness.
notes: The 'button' metaphor for clitoris appears in many world languages; زر is also the everyday Arabic word for doorbell and shirt button; functions similarly to English 'clit' in register — informal but not maximally offensive.

definition: Colloquial slang for the clitoris literally meaning 'grain,' 'bead,' or 'pea'; emphasizes the small rounded protrusion of the clitoral glans.
notes: حبة has many primary meanings: grain, pill, pimple, pea, bead; the clitoris sense is context-dependent; the diminutive-size connotation softens the crudeness compared to more direct terms.

definition: The standard clinical Arabic term for a single testicle; the primary anatomical noun used in medical and formal health contexts.
notes: Classical Arabic medical term; singular form — dual الخصيتان and plural الخصى are more common in actual discourse; carries social taboo in lay speech despite clinical status.

definition: The standard clinical Arabic dual form for 'the two testicles' with the definite article; used in medical and anatomical discourse to refer to both testes as a paired anatomical unit.
notes: Arabic's grammatical dual number makes this the natural clinical form; preferred in urology, reproductive medicine, and anatomy education; the definite article reflects anatomical specificity.

definition: Clinical Arabic dual term for the testicles literally meaning 'the two eggs'; used in both medical and lay contexts, reflecting an ancient pan-Semitic metaphor.
notes: The 'egg' (بيضة) = testicle metaphor is ancient and pan-Semitic; appears in classical texts including Quranic commentary; more accessible to lay speakers than الخصيتان because بيضة (egg) is an everyday word.

definition: The clinical Arabic compound term for the scrotum, literally 'the testicular sac'; used in urological and anatomical texts.
notes: Compound of كيس (sac/bag) + الصفن (the scrotum); the compound form is more common in medical writing than the bare noun صفن alone; low lay recognition because the anatomical root صفن is itself rare in everyday speech.

definition: The primary classical Arabic anatomical noun for the scrotum; the scrotal pouch encasing the testes and epididymides.
notes: Pure specialist medical terminology; almost entirely absent from lay speech; documented in classical Arabic medical texts (Ibn Sina and others) and modern anatomical literature; among the lowest-recognition terms in this dataset.

definition: The most universally recognized colloquial Arabic slang for testicles, literally 'eggs'; moderately crude and understood across all dialect zones.
notes: Plural of بيضة (egg); distinguished from the clinical البيضتان by the absence of the definite article and dual morphology; widely used in expressions for 'kick in the balls' and metaphorically for courage; recognized by virtually all adult Arabic speakers.

definition: Crude dialectal slang for testicles emphasizing spherical shape; used as an insult intensifier as well as a literal anatomical reference.
notes: Likely related to the root for 'sphere'; most prevalent in Gulf and Iraqi dialects; used in insults and frustration expressions; less pan-Arabic than بيض or كرات.

definition: Colloquial slang for testicles literally meaning 'beads' or 'glass beads'; uses the bead metaphor for the smooth rounded shape of the testes.
notes: Primary meaning is decorative glass or stone beads; the testicle metaphor extends this to smooth rounded objects; less widely recognized as genital slang than بيض or كرات; dialectal distribution strongest in Levantine Arabic.

definition: Crude slang for testicles meaning 'stones' or 'rocks'; parallels the English 'stones' metaphor, emphasizing hardness, solidity, and weight.
notes: Plural of حجر (stone/rock); the 'stones' metaphor for testicles appears cross-linguistically; also used metaphorically for courage; present across Levantine, Gulf, and North African dialects.

definition: Widely-used colloquial slang for testicles literally meaning 'balls' (spheres); directly parallels English 'balls' in meaning, crudeness level, and metaphorical extension to courage.
notes: Plural of كرة (ball/sphere); used in expressions equivalent to 'break my balls' (تكسر كراتي = you're annoying me) and for courage; one of the most widely recognized testicle slang terms across all Arabic dialects.

definition: The standard classical and clinical Arabic term for the breast or mammary gland; used in medical, anatomical, and formal health contexts for the breast in both sexes.
notes: Classical Arabic term documented in the Quran and classical literature primarily in lactation contexts; plural is أثداء (athdāʾ); carries cultural sensitivity in public discourse despite clinical status; widely recognized by all adult speakers.

definition: The standard Arabic word for 'chest'; in sexual or romantic contexts functions as a socially acceptable euphemism for the female breasts, referencing the anterior thoracic area rather than the mammary glands specifically.
notes: Extremely common word with multiple meanings: chest (body part), front/head of an organization, and emotional bosom; used widely in poetry and colloquial speech as a modesty-preserving alternative to ثدي; suitable for mixed-company speech where ثدي would feel clinical or awkward.
